audit_findings.title: Post-2025 rig sales break the earnings perimeter and may double-count proceeds
audit_findings.magnitude: $424.0m aggregate sale price ($274.0m cash and $150.0m seller notes); $206.4m net disposal proceeds received in H1 2026; $150.0m notes receivable omitted from the bridge; disposed-rig OE unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The DCF capitalizes 2025 OE from a pre-sale fleet, while the bridge adds June 2026 cash containing disposal proceeds but omits the separately recorded seller notes.
audit_findings.evidence: On December 8, 2025, Noble announced that the Company signed definitive agreements to sell six jackup rigs, which includes the sale of five rigs to Borr Drilling Limited (“Borr”) for $ 360.0 million and a separate transaction for the sale of one rig to Ocean Oilfield Drilling for $ 64.0 million in cash.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, although the net valuation error is not. Capitalizing earnings from sold rigs would overstate value, while omitting the $150.0m notes receivable understates value by $0.93 per diluted share. The rig-specific sustainable OE and treatment of the remaining $64.0m sale are not established, so the net direction remains mixed and could materially affect the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild anchor OE for the retained fleet, include only post-sale bareboat-charter economics, reconcile the $206.4m H1 disposal proceeds to June cash, add the $150.0m notes receivable at appropriate economic value, and incorporate the Noble Resolve consideration only when received or otherwise recognized.

audit_findings.title: Current cash taxes may understate the sustainable tax burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $250.6m recurring 2025 tax accruals versus $121.129m cash taxes paid, a $129.471m difference; sustainable adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A cash-flow-derived OE anchor reflects taxes paid, while the DCF perpetuates that anchor without an explicit adjustment for deferred or timing-related cash-tax obligations.
audit_findings.evidence: Such tax benefits were offset by various recurring annual accruals of $ 250.6 million primarily in Guyana, the United States, Switzerland, and Luxembourg.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed cash-tax and recurring-accrual amounts demonstrate a large timing mismatch equal to 33.4% of the $387.7m anchor. They do not prove that OE should be reduced by the full $129.471m, but the scale is plainly capable of changing value materially if a substantial portion becomes recurring cash tax.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the 2025 OE tax deduction to the $121.129m paid, the $250.6m recurring accruals, deferred taxes, uncertain-tax-position movements, attribute utilization and expiry; then rerun all scenarios using a supported steady-state cash-tax charge.

audit_findings.title: Unresolved tax claims are a non-debt claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.5m outstanding audit claims at June 30, 2026; $119.1m uncertain-tax-position reserves
audit_findings.mechanism: Any settlement not represented in normalized OE would require a bridge deduction or an explicit forward cash-flow charge ahead of common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: Audit claims of approximately $ 351.4 million at December 31, 2025, attributable to income and other business taxes remain outstanding and are under continued objection by Noble.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing reduces outstanding audit claims from $351.4m to $11.5m. That current claim equals about $0.07 per diluted share and 0.2% of the $5.903bn base equity value. Even the separate $119.1m uncertain-tax-position reserve equals only about $0.74 per share and 2.0% of base value, insufficient on the supplied valuation ranges to change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the $11.5m claim is included in the $119.1m reserve and whether any related deposits or indemnities exist; prevent double counting, and rerun only if updated expected exposure materially exceeds these filed amounts.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease principal can bypass both OE capex and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $23.936m paid in 2025, $62.526m paid in H1 2026, and $19.812m current finance-lease liability at June 30, 2026; sustainable amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Finance-lease amortization can be added back with D&A while principal is classified as financing cash flow and therefore omitted from both operating cash flow and reported cash capex; the bridge also does not deduct the lease liability.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, we repurchased 0.7 million of our Ordinary Shares for a total of $20.0 million, made dividend payments to our shareholders of $320.4 million, made finance lease payments of $23.9 million, and paid $9.7 million in taxes withheld on vested employee share-based compensation awards.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed payments demonstrate a real equipment-related cash cost that can bypass a conventional cash-flow OE calculation. The 2025 payment equals 6.2% of anchor OE, but the record indicates conversion of specific BOP leases into owned equipment and does not establish that this payment level is recurring. Materiality of the sustainable adjustment therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace lease amortization, interest, principal, the $73.0m BOP purchase program and noncash asset transfers through the OE calculation; charge recurring economic equipment cost to OE and capture any remaining liability once, then rerun if the normalized annual adjustment is material.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 capex base may be below the forward requirement
audit_findings.magnitude: $615.0m-$665.0m 2026 estimate versus $519.523m 2025 cash capex, an increase of $95.477m-$145.477m; H1 2026 cash capex was $308.383m
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation grows 2025 OE without explicitly reflecting higher sustaining, survey, reactivation or contract-upgrade capital requirements.
audit_findings.evidence: Our total capital expenditures estimate for 2026 is expected to range between $590.0 million and $640.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The disclosed increase equals 24.6%-37.5% of the $387.7m anchor and is large enough to change the valuation materially if a meaningful portion is required to sustain existing earnings. The filing does not establish how much is maintenance versus value-creating growth, so the full increase is not a demonstrated OE reduction.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the 2026 forecast and actual spending by sustaining, survey, reactivation, contract-upgrade, rebillable and expansion categories, exclude divested-rig spending, incorporate finance-lease purchases, and rerun all scenarios using normalized sustaining capex.

audit_findings.title: Acquisitions contaminate the OE trend used to support growth
audit_findings.magnitude: Diamond contributed $336.542m of revenue from September 4 through December 31, 2024, while the 2025 revenue increase included $626.2m from acquired floaters; OE effect unquantified; base exceeds bear by $835m or $5.15 per share and bull exceeds bear by $1.471bn or $9.08 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Partial-year and full-year acquisition contributions inflate the reported OE trend used to justify the 3%-5% growth assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: The results of Diamond operations were included in the Company’s results of operations effective on the Diamond Closing Date.
audit_findings.explanation: The mixed acquisition perimeter is demonstrated, although its precise OE effect is unavailable. Growth is valuation-material: moving from the 0% bear case to the 3% base case adds $5.15 per share, while the 5% bull case adds $9.08 per share. Without a same-fleet pro forma series, the reported trend cannot establish that this increase is organic or repeatable.
audit_findings.action: Construct a full-period pro forma OE series for the retained fleet, remove purchase-accounting contract amortization, integration costs and sold-rig contributions, identify realized synergies separately, and rerun the growth cases using the resulting organic trend.
